messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — opened a docs PR to sync SDK snippets across Python/TypeScript/Go for the new streaming + pagination + retry semantics. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482
Samir Patel: Looking now. Quick Q — should the Python streaming example switch fully to async iterators (`async for`) in all snippets, or keep a callback example for users on older runtimes?
Maya Chen: We deprecated the callback in SDK v0.12, so I changed the canonical snippet to async iterator. Example included in the PR:
```py
# Python (async iterator streaming)
async for chunk in client.chat.stream(request):
    print(chunk.delta)
```
Jo Alvarez: For TypeScript I added both variants: the event emitter style (`stream.on('data', ...)`) and the `for await (const ...)` async iterator example so docs show migration paths. Also clarified retry policy config with a short table and an example: `retry: { policy: 'default', max_attempts: 3 }`.
Samir Patel: Go has a slightly different shape — in the Go SDK `Stream()` now returns a receive-only channel. Proposed Go snippet in the PR:
```go
// Go (channel streaming)
stream := client.ChatStream(ctx, req)
for msg := range stream {
    fmt.Println(msg.Delta)
}
```
Jo Alvarez: Important note added about pagination cursors: cursors are not guaranteed to be stable across model variants/quantization; added a short recommendation to store opaque tokens and re-run a small validation query after a model switch.
Maya Chen: CI just flagged a docs-lint failure on one of the fenced codeblock language tags (python vs py). devx-bot reported it: :x:
devx-bot: CI / docs-lint — failed — https://ci.redwood/dev/482
Samir Patel: I'll push a lint fix in a minute (normalize all fences to triple backticks with the canonical language). Also adding an explicit migration section at the top: `/docs/migration/sdk-0.12-streaming.md` that lists the breaking snippets and translation tips.
Oliver King: Assign me for final review after the lint fix, @Maya Chen. Also can we add a tiny extractor test that validates all code fences parse as the declared language (so we don't regress on the CI lint)?
Maya Chen: Good call. I'll add a lightweight pytest that scans the markdown in the PR for code fences and asserts supported languages only (py, ts, go). Will push the test and the lint fixes — ETA EOD. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: After Maya pushes, I'll re-run the local docs build and spot-check the rendered examples (live stream + pagination integration).
Oliver King: Sounds good. Once green, I'll do final approval and merge. Thanks all for the quick sync — moving this out of WIP today.
